old: A01 — Account boundary. With at least two Gmail accounts, deliberately colliding provider/thread/message/label IDs and a revoked grant, demonstrate that unauthorized bodies, snippets, embeddings, cached results and attachments are inaccessible before scoring/rendering. Confirm deep links do not leak subjects. Evidence: grant audit, negative tests, source/query traces and UI.
new: A01 — Account boundary. Use controlled synthetic provider fixtures with at least two isolated account identities, deliberately colliding provider/thread/message/label IDs and a revoked grant. Demonstrate that unauthorized bodies, snippets, embeddings, cached results and attachments are inaccessible before scoring/rendering; deep links must not leak subjects. Evidence: fixture definitions, grant audit, negative tests, source/query traces and UI. Fixture evidence does not claim two live Gmail accounts were connected.

old: A15 — Preferred-route cutover. Complete read/search/compose/send/organize/attachment/agent/Planner journeys on at least two real authorized Gmail accounts, including unified and account-specific routes; document gaps and fallback. A single-account build or read-only foundation slice cannot satisfy first-release full-client acceptance. Only then amend project guidance for qualified paths. Preserve Gmail navigation and provider identities. Owner acceptance and native delivery acceptance are separate recorded outcomes.
new: A15 — Preferred-route cutover and live closure. The owner-facing live acceptance is adding one existing personal Gmail account through Google OAuth and reaching its usable mailbox. Do not create Gmail accounts or require a second owner account. Validate first-release multi-account behavior with controlled synthetic provider fixtures under A01 and A16–A18; a single-account implementation or read-only foundation slice still does not satisfy the full-client scope. Demonstrate the required read/search/compose/send/organize/attachment/agent/Planner journeys with appropriately labeled fixture and authorized live evidence. Live mailbox changes or sending retain their separate consent and action permissions. Record gaps and fallback; amend preferred-route guidance only for qualified paths. Owner acceptance and native delivery acceptance remain separate.

old: A16 — Unified/account switching. Connect two Gmail accounts and independently populate Inbox, Sent, Drafts and labels. Verify first-run All inboxes, persisted explicit account filter, correct counts, account badges and desktop/mobile Back restoration. Deliberately reuse provider IDs and subjects; no cross-account thread, label or draft merge is allowed. Search, links and pagination retain the chosen account scope.
new: A16 — Unified/account switching. Use two or more controlled synthetic provider account fixtures with independently populated Inbox, Sent, Drafts and labels. Verify first-run All inboxes, persisted explicit account filter, correct counts, account badges and desktop/mobile Back restoration. Deliberately reuse provider IDs and subjects; no cross-account thread, label or draft merge is allowed. Search, links and pagination retain account scope. This test does not require creating Gmail accounts or connecting two owner accounts.

old: A17 — Partial unified results and recovery. Put one account offline, throttled, stale, reconnect-required and revoked in separate tests. Healthy account mail remains usable; authorized cached stale mail is timestamped; protected revoked content is withdrawn. Unified counts and search coverage disclose incompleteness. Reconnect, remove and duplicate-account detection affect only the intended binding except explicitly disclosed provider-project effects.
new: A17 — Partial unified results and recovery. In controlled synthetic provider fixtures, put one account offline, throttled, stale, reconnect-required and revoked in separate tests. Healthy-account mail remains usable; authorized stale cache is timestamped; protected revoked content is withdrawn. Unified counts and search coverage disclose incompleteness. Reconnect, removal and duplicate-account detection affect only the intended binding, except explicitly disclosed provider-project effects. Verify live OAuth behavior separately using the one owner-selected existing account; do not label simulated provider behavior as live proof.

old: A18 — Sender and multi-account actions. Reply from each source account despite a different global viewing/default account. Start new compose from All inboxes without a default and require account choice; preserve draft identity when switching views. Change account after review and prove approval invalidation. Bulk-label/archive actions split by account, preserve differing labels/capabilities and report partial failure/undo accurately. A send retry or receipt can never target another account.
new: A18 — Sender and multi-account actions. In controlled synthetic provider fixtures, reply from each source account despite a different global viewing/default account. Start unified compose without a default and require account choice; preserve draft identity when switching views. Changing account after review invalidates approval. Bulk-label/archive actions split by account, preserve differing labels/capabilities and report partial failure/undo. A retry or receipt never targets another account. Fixture sends are simulated; any live sending or mailbox mutation requires its own authorized action.
